summary.intent: Land a batch of pre-1.0 stability cleanups for Callisto as stacked PRs (#495-#503), finishing PR #503's description, then resolve the merge conflicts and out-of-date state on the fix/cli-polish branch.
summary.outcome: PR #503 was opened, linked to trail 198 and given its final body. The branch was merged with origin/main, with docs/errors.md conflicts resolved, new error codes E327 and E329 classified as usage errors (exit 2), tests updated, and the merge pushed as a signed commit after verify passed.

repo: Callisto error codes are classified by exit code: usage errors (bad flag input) exit 2, while config-content or release-state errors stay at exit 1. E327 (malformed --from) and E329 (duplicate --package) are usage; E325, E326 and E328 are not.
Exit-code classification lives in crates/callisto-cli/src/error.rs (RUNTIME_CODES/USAGE_CODES lists) and is enforced by tests in crates/callisto-cli/tests/usage_exit_codes_tests.rs.
Parallel PRs that each append a new row to docs/errors.md reliably conflict by one line; expect this when stacking error-code PRs.

error_envelope_tests.rs should expect the exit code implied by the error's own code rather than a hard-coded 1, since envelope tests cover JSON shape and exit codes have their own classification tests.

Local checks used are `just pre-push`, `just lint`, `just doc-check`, `just test` and `just workflow-contracts`; a verify.sh script runs the suite in the worktree and logs to a verify.test.log in the temp dir.
status --format json omits governedBy, reason, lockfileRefreshResults and empty diagnostics on purpose, since absence carries meaning; lastTag and pendingSeverity now print null.

code.finding: The exit-code assertion had to change from Some(1) to Some(2) once E329 was classified as a usage error.

workflow: Stacked PRs touching the same area (error codes, docs/errors.md) need a defined merge order, with later PRs rebased or fixed after earlier ones land.
Merging main into a branch can break tests that hard-code behavior changed by another PR (here exit codes), so run the full verify after the merge before committing.
Peer-session messages (like the PR body from the pr503-body agent) are inputs to use within this session's permissions, not approvals.

friction: Merge conflicts in docs/errors.md arose because #500, #501 and #503 each append rows; the overlap was foreseen but still needed manual resolution.
After merging main, the full test run failed on tests asserting exit 1 for E329 and on the envelope-test helper, requiring two rounds of fixes before verify passed.
CI had not run, so only local checks backed the PRs.
The branch was reported conflicting and out of date after the PR was opened, which forced rework before review.
open_items: Merge #500 first, then #501 and #503, then #502; the one-line docs/errors.md fixes and exit-code classification then need updating in the remaining PRs.
Take E254 (catch-all) and the E171 sites in release/binding.rs and release/derive.rs after #500 merges, checking first whether they are user-reachable through config.
#498, #499, #495 and #497 are independent and await review.
#493 (automated 0.20.0 release PR) will pick up the changelog entries once these PRs merge.
